config-core.title: Company name with a line break injects code into the generated client.config.js, which vite.config.js runs in Node
config-core.evidence: The header is built as `// ${config.client?.name || 'SolarFlow client'} - SolarFlow settings`, and the name is not escaped. In submission.js:91 the name comes from the client's payload: `const company = String(contact.company || '').trim()`. trim() only strips the ends, so line breaks inside the name survive. validateClientConfig (resolve.js) only checks that the name is not empty, and setup_save accepts any string. template/vite.config.js:4 runs `import clientConfig from './src/config/client.config.js'`, so the module is executed in Node by `npm run dev` / `npm run build`. It is also bundled into the client app. I tested this in /tmp/bsec/inj.mjs: emptySubmission() with contact.company = "Acme Solar\nglobalThis.PWNED='yes';//", then submissionToClientConfig, then clientConfigSource, then import(). The result was checkClientConfig errors [] and globalThis.PWNED === 'yes'. The same thing happens with \r, U+2028 and U+2029. U+2028 can even be pasted into a normal single-line input.
config-core.scenario: Anyone holding a setup link (the client, or someone the WhatsApp link was forwarded to) saves contact.company = "Sun Power require('child_process')... //". They can do this through the wizard or directly with supabase.rpc('setup_save'). The admin clicks Download zip and gets no validation error. When the agency or the client's CI runs `npm run build` on the zip, vite.config.js imports client.config.js and the injected code runs on that machine with the user's privileges. It also ships in the browser bundle of the client CRM.
config-core.final_fix: Keep client text out of the comment header, or write it as JSON.stringify(name) after removing [\r\n  ]. In validateClientConfig, reject control characters and U+2028/U+2029 in client.name and in every label and option. Add a test that imports the serialized module built from a hostile name and checks that nothing outside `export default` runs.
config-core.verify_reasoning: Reproduced on my own in /tmp/vsec/t1.mjs. serialize.js:9 puts config.client.name raw into a `//` comment. submission.js:83 only trims the ends of contact.company, and validateClientConfig (resolve.js:312) only checks that the name is not empty. A company of "Acme globalThis.X=1;//" gave checkClientConfig errors [] and, once the serialized module was imported, globalThis.X === 1. build.js buildClientFiles writes this exact source to src/config/client.config.js. template/vite.config.js:4 imports that file, so the code runs in Node on every `npm run dev` or `npm run build` of the zip, and it also ships in the client bundle. Admin overrides (slug, ownerEmail, branding) cannot change client.name, so the admin has no chance to clean it. U+2028 survives a single-line text input, and setup_save accepts any JSON. The attacker is anyone holding the invite link, and the victim is the agency's or client's build machine, so this is critical.

The stock deduction trigger checks feature_on('inventory') (schema.sql:1011).

'Vendor' now appears in the Staff logins role list, but creating one fails with 'vendor logins are switched off for this company'. config-core.title: Owner email goes unescaped into a SQL snippet in the client README
config-core.evidence: README line 98 reads: `update public.profiles set user_type = 'admin' ... where lower(email) = lower('{{OWNER_EMAIL}}');`. OWNER_EMAIL is filled verbatim (build.js fillReadme / seed.js README_PLACEHOLDERS). It defaults to the client-entered contact.email (submission.js:107). The only check is /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/, which allows quotes, semicolons and /**/ comments. setup.sql itself escapes the value correctly (sqlText, which I tested in PGlite), but this snippet does not.
config-core.scenario: contact.email = "o'brien@sun.in" (a valid address) gives `lower('o'brien@sun.in')`, a syntax error in the fix-up instructions. A crafted value such as `x');delete/**/from/**/public.profiles;--@a.co` passes validation and becomes a destructive statement that the owner or agency is told to paste into the SQL Editor.
config-core.final_fix: Add an SQL-escaped placeholder (for example OWNER_EMAIL_SQL = value.replaceAll("'", "''")) for that snippet, and reject quotes, semicolons and backslashes in the owner email.
config-core.verify_reasoning: README.client.md:98 embeds {{OWNER_EMAIL}} inside lower('...') in a SQL snippet. seed.js:17 fills it verbatim, and the only validation is /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ (resolve.js:315), which allows quotes, semicolons and /**/. A legitimate o'brien@x.in therefore produces a broken statement. A crafted email can turn into extra statements, but only in a troubleshooting step that a human copies by hand into the client's own project, where the address would look visibly strange. builder.title: After a save conflict, Send submits the other tab's draft and shows 'Thank you'; this tab's edits are dropped silently
builder.evidence: When a save conflicts, setConflict(true), so `enabled: ready && !conflict && !linkGone` becomes false. In useAutosave (template/src/ui hooks), disabled means `savedRef.current = null`, `status: enabled ? status : 'saved'` and unsaved=false. So the status line says Saved and the beforeunload guard is removed. `flush = () => enabledRef.current ? persist(...) : Promise.resolve(true)` then resolves true without saving anything. send() (line 150) does `if (!(await flush())) throw ...; await submitSetup(...)`, and setup_submit snapshots whatever draft is on the server.
builder.scenario: The client has the form open on a phone and a laptop. The laptop saves first. The phone's next edit hits 'conflict'. The client ignores the banner (the save status still reads Saved), keeps editing on the phone and taps Send. flush() returns true, the server snapshots the laptop's older draft as the submission, and the phone shows the Done screen. None of the phone's answers reach the agency, and closing the tab gives no warning.
builder.final_fix: Have flush return false while conflict or linkGone is set (or check those flags in send() before submitting), and disable the Send button with a clear message. Report status 'error' or 'unsaved' instead of 'saved' while disabled with local edits pending, and keep the beforeunload guard. Optionally re-fetch the server draft on conflict and offer overwrite or merge.
builder.verify_reasoning: SetupWizard.jsx:105 passes enabled: ready && !conflict && !linkGone. In useAutosave (template/src/ui/hooks.js), disabled sets savedRef to null, returns status 'saved' and makes unsaved false, which removes the beforeunload guard. flush() then resolves true without saving. send() (SetupWizard.jsx ~150) only checks flush() and then calls submitSetup, and setup_submit snapshots whatever draft is on the server (builder.sql insert into submissions from d.payload). So after a conflict, Send succeeds and shows Done, and any edits made in this tab after the conflict are never sent. One mitigating point: a red 'changed in another tab — reload' banner stays at the top of the page, so the user is warned visually, but Send is not blocked.

builder.title: A link holder can grow submissions without limit, making the admin page very large
builder.evidence: setup_submit inserts a new submissions row for every new draft version. The only cap is 256 KB per payload and 120 calls per minute per invite. setup_admin_get (lines 348-350) returns every submission's full payload, with no limit. In /tmp/bsec/spam.mjs, 30 rounds of save+submit with a 250 KB notes field produced 30 submissions, and setup_admin_get returned 7,759,137 bytes.
builder.scenario: A malicious or buggy client with the link runs save+submit in a loop: about 60 snapshots, roughly 15 MB, per minute, indefinitely. The builder database fills up, and the admin client page has to download and parse hundreds of MB, so it becomes unusable for that invite.
builder.final_fix: Keep only the last N submissions per invite (or cap the count), rate-limit submit separately, and have setup_admin_get return submission metadata, with payloads fetched one at a time on demand.
builder.verify_reasoning: setup_submit inserts (invite_id, d.version, d.payload) with on conflict on (invite_id, version) only. Every save bumps the version, so alternating save and submit adds a new row each time. The only limits are the 256 KB payload cap and the per-invite call rate limit. Submitting stays allowed after status 'submitted' (resend). setup_admin_get aggregates every submission's full payload with no limit. Growth is about 60 snapshots, roughly 15 MB, per minute per invite. It needs a hostile link holder, and the admin can archive the invite to stop it, so low is right.

Both the count and the export only select rows with a registration_date. The only editor for registration_date is RegistrationTab.jsx:40; a grep of src shows no other writer. REGISTRATION is `removable: true` (stages.js:28), and stageLocks() does not lock it, so the builder lets a client drop it.
app-lists.scenario: Config (c): pipeline without REGISTRATION and dataExports on (the default). The admin opens Data Exports and picks any period. The count shows 0, and Export shows 'No registered projects were found in this date range.' for every range, so the feature cannot export anything.
app-lists.final_fix: When !isStageEnabled(STAGE_IDS.REGISTRATION), filter and order by created_at (an IST timestamp range, as filters.js does for Leads), and relabel the UI and filename from 'registrations' to 'projects'. Alternatively add requiresStages: ['REGISTRATION'] to dataExports so the builder locks the stage.
app-lists.verify_reasoning: DataExportView.jsx:70 filters both the count and the export by gte/lte('registration_date'). A grep of template/src and template/backend finds only one writer of registration_date: RegistrationTab.jsx:40. No trigger, AddLeadModal path or import sets it. REGISTRATION is `removable: true` (stages.js:28). dataExports has no requiresStages (features.js:171), so stageLocks() never locks REGISTRATION and resolveFeaturesAndPipeline keeps dataExports on. Without the Registration stage every range therefore counts 0, and Export shows 'No registered projects were found in this date range.' The whole feature is useless for that config, but it is a secondary feature with no data loss, so I grade it medium, not high.

app-lists.title: Year filter empties every non-Leads stage list, and 'Registered today' is always 0, when Registration is removed
app-lists.evidence: `const field = isLeads ? 'created_at' : 'registration_date';`. The YearSelect is shown for every stage (Dashboard.jsx:589), and the stage query applies these ranges (Dashboard.jsx:214). queries.js:54 counts `eq('registration_date', today)` for the 'Registered today' tile, which DashboardView.jsx:115 always shows.
app-lists.scenario: Config (c), REGISTRATION removed. Open the 'Site Survey' or 'Material Order' list and pick year 2026: the list is empty even though customers are there, because registration_date is null on every record. The Dashboard 'Registered today' tile shows 0 forever.
app-lists.final_fix: In stageDateFilters use created_at (IST timestamp bounds) when !isStageEnabled(STAGE_IDS.REGISTRATION). Hide the 'Registered today' tile, or switch it to 'Added today' on created_at, when Registration is off.
app-lists.verify_reasoning: filters.js:37 uses 'registration_date' for every non-Leads stage. Dashboard.jsx:213-215 applies those ranges, and the YearSelect is shown for every stage list (Dashboard.jsx:589). yearFilter defaults to '' (Dashboard.jsx:76), so lists are only emptied once a year is picked, but then every non-Leads list is empty because registration_date is never written without the Registration tab. queries.js:54 counts eq('registration_date', today), and DashboardView.jsx:115 always shows that tile, so it stays at 0.

app-lists.title: Exports write raw stage ids instead of the client's stage names
app-lists.evidence: exportColumns maps 'stage' to `{ key, label: titleCase(key) }` with no getter, so the cell is the stored id.
app-lists.scenario: Config (c) renamed LEADS to 'Enquiries' and MATERIAL DELIVERY to 'Dispatch'. The CSV/Excel stage column shows 'LEADS' / 'MATERIAL DELIVERY'.
app-lists.final_fix: Import stageLabel and give the stage column `get: row => stageLabel(row.stage)`, for example by special-casing key === 'stage' in the builtIn map.
app-lists.verify_reasoning: exportColumns (DataExportView.jsx:45) maps built-in keys to { key, label } with no getter. toCsv (lib/download.js:18) and the Excel cell function fall back to row[column.key], so the stage column holds raw ids such as 'LEADS' or 'MATERIAL DELIVERY' instead of the client's renamed labels.

app-lists.title: Permanent delete removes the documents rows but leaves the files in the customer-documents bucket
app-lists.evidence: handleHardDelete runs only `supabase.from('admin').delete()`. documents rows go with it via `on delete cascade`, but nothing calls storage.remove for `<customer id>/...`. The storage policies require an existing admin row, so the files become unreachable from the app and are never cleaned up.
app-lists.scenario: Admin permanently deletes a customer with 10 uploaded Aadhaar/PAN scans. The scans stay in storage indefinitely, still taking up the bucket quota, and the CRM has no way to find or remove them.
app-lists.final_fix: In handleHardDelete, select the documents' storage_path values for the customer first (or list the `<id>/` prefix), then call `supabase.storage.from('customer-documents').remove(paths)` while the admin row still exists, because the policies need it. Then delete the row. Report any files that could not be removed. Alternatively, do it atomically in a server-side Edge Function with the service role.
app-lists.verify_reasoning: handleHardDelete (Dashboard.jsx:419-428) only deletes the admin row. documents rows cascade away (schema.sql:233), and backend/ has no trigger or function that removes storage.objects. The only storage remove in the app is single-document delete (utils.jsx:774). All storage policies require an existing admin row whose id matches the folder (schema.sql:1486-1499), so after the delete nobody in the app can list, read or remove the files. Personal ID scans (Aadhaar/PAN) stay retained in the bucket indefinitely, reachable only with the service role. That is storage waste plus PII retention after a deletion the user believes is permanent. No breakage in the app itself.

app-lists.title: Partner-office logins trigger metadata inserts that RLS always refuses
app-lists.evidence: syncMetadata runs after every successful handleUpdateCustomer for all Dashboard roles, CPO and office2 included, and inserts new module_brand/channel_partner labels. The metadata_write policy is is_head_office() only, so the insert fails and is only logged with console.warn.
app-lists.scenario: A CPO types a new module brand 'XYZ' on a customer. The customer saves, but 'XYZ' never joins the dropdown list, so the brand does not appear in the list or in the Operations counts.
app-lists.final_fix: Skip syncMetadata unless the user is head office (admin/sales). If partner offices should be able to propose names, add a security-definer RPC that inserts into metadata with validation.
app-lists.verify_reasoning: syncMetadata (Dashboard.jsx:312-324) runs after every successful update (:372) for all Dashboard types, including channel_partner_office and office2 (App.jsx:15). The metadata_write policy is is_head_office() only (schema.sql:1411-1413), so the insert always fails for those roles and is only logged with console.warn. The behaviour matches the claim, but the effect is small and partly by design: only head office curates the lists. The record keeps its value, and the cost is a pointless failing request plus a custom brand that is never offered in the dropdown, with no message telling the user. Low.

app-lists.title: Customers sitting in a stage that is later removed vanish from every list and cannot be advanced
app-lists.evidence: getNextStageId returns null when `PRIMARY_STAGES.findIndex(...) === -1`. Sidebar.jsx only renders STAGE_GROUPS. DashboardView's 'Projects by stage' iterates PRIMARY_STAGES. CustomerDetailModal resolveTab falls back to LEADS, so no 'Save & Move' appears (it needs activeTab === customer.stage).
app-lists.scenario: A client upgrades with a new zip where loanTracking is off (README 'Upgrading an existing install') while 20 customers have stage='LOAN'. Those 20 are counted in Total projects but appear in no sidebar list or stage bar. Opened via global search, they show the Leads tab with no move button. The only escape is Pause, which resumes to Leads.
app-lists.final_fix: Add an 'Other / not in pipeline' list (stage not in STAGE_BY_ID and not terminal), and in the modal offer a move to the first applicable stage after the record's old position, or let admins choose any stage. Optionally have setup.sql or the admin page report counts of rows whose stage is outside the new pipeline.
app-lists.verify_reasoning: getNextStageId returns null when the current stage is not in PRIMARY_STAGES (config/index.js:57-58). Sidebar.jsx:111 renders only STAGE_GROUPS, and DashboardView.jsx:217 iterates only PRIMARY_STAGES. CustomerDetailModal resolveTab (lines 191-194) falls back to LEADS because isTabAvailable needs STAGE_BY_ID, so Save & Move (needing activeTab === customer.stage and nextStageId) never shows. The card override (CustomerCard.jsx:219) is only reachable from stage lists, which never list these records. The README upgrade path (README.client.md:103-110) runs the new setup.sql and does nothing about existing rows in removed stages. Only global search reaches them, and Pause is the only escape. This applies only to upgrades that drop a stage, so medium.
